servers.risk_summary: The agent-council OpenClaw skill presents a low-to-moderate risk profile consistent with a legitimate multi-agent orchestration toolkit. All three Semgrep medium findings are false positives in context — standard urllib API calls to Discord's REST API — and the provenance flags (47-day account age, no lockfile) are non-compounding and expected in the young OpenClaw ecosystem. No encoded payloads, credential harvesting, silent persistence, or malicious instruction patterns were identified in the current version; residual risk is limited to standard supply chain hygiene concerns applicable to any network-capable open-source tool.

openclaw-sec is a substantive security detection library whose high-severity SAST findings are overwhelmingly false positives arising from scanner context collapse — the tool's own detection patterns and test fixtures are being flagged as live credentials and malicious code. The primary residual risk is the unaudited hook installation mechanism (user-prompt-submit-hook.ts, tool-call-hook.ts, install-hooks.sh), which installs persistent hooks intercepting all agent interactions and whose source code is not present in the scan evidence. A 47-day-old account publishing a security tool with persistent hook capabilities warrants conditional approval pending hook code review.

The auto-updater skill contains zero scanner findings, no malicious instruction patterns, and uses only official first-party Clawdbot/ClawdHub tooling with transparent, documented cron scheduling via the official platform API. The sole substantive concern — that a daily automated update mechanism creates a standing trust dependency on the clawdhub registry and clawdbot npm package — is an architectural property inherent to all auto-update mechanisms, not a vulnerability specific to this skill. Users should understand they are granting ongoing automated update authority to these upstream registries before enabling this skill.

The pskoett/self-improving-agent OpenClaw skill presents a clean security profile with no critical, high, medium, or low findings. All four scanner findings are informational-severity SKILL_CHMOD_EXEC false positives located in a troubleshooting reference document, consistent with standard CLI tool installation practice. The only residual concern is a theoretical hook persistence supply chain risk requiring multiple simultaneous conditions, which does not rise to a blocking or advisory level.

This package is a sophisticated AI agent self-evolution framework with documented autonomous execution, programmatic npm install without audit flags, and a self-modification capability ('Mad Dog Mode') that represents genuinely elevated risk. The majority of SAST findings are false positives contextually appropriate to the tool's stated purpose, but two substantive concerns remain: the programmatic npm install with --no-audit in skills_monitor.js and an unverified split chain of custody between the 'openclaw' registry owner and the 'autogame-17' GitHub account that controls the update stream. No confirmed malicious payload, obfuscated code, or C2 indicators are present, but the architecture is weaponizable and the external trust anchor (autogame-17) has unverified provenance.
